<ns0:uscDoc xmlns:ns0="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0 USLM-1.0.15.xsd" xml:lang="en" identifier="/us/usc/t20"><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf5-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definitions</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">In this chapter:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf6-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Individualized education program</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf7-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">The term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bf8-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bf9-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> how the child’s disability affects the child’s involvement and progress in the general education curriculum;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfa-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for preschool children, as appropriate, how the disability affects the child’s participation in appropriate activities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfb-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bfc-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals, designed to—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfd-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> meet the child’s needs that result from the child’s disability to enable the child to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfe-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> meet each of the child’s other educational needs that result from the child’s disability;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bff-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a description of how the child’s progress toward meeting the annual goals described in subclause (II) will be measured and when periodic reports on the progress the child is making toward meeting the annual goals (such as through the use of quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with the issuance of report cards) will be provided;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c00-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV"><ns0:num value="IV">(IV)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services, based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, to be provided to the child, or on behalf of the child, and a statement of the program modifications or supports for school personnel that will be provided for the child—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c01-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to advance appropriately toward attaining the annual goals;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c02-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum in accordance with subclause (I) and to participate in extracurricular and other nonacademic activities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c03-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children in the activities described in this subparagraph;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c04-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/V"><ns0:num value="V">(V)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and in the activities described in subclause (IV)(cc);</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c05-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI"><ns0:num value="VI">(VI)</ns0:num><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c06-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1412/a/16/A">section 1412(a)(16)(A) of this title</ns0:ref>; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c07-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> if the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subitem style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c08-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb/AA"><ns0:num value="AA">(AA)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the child cannot participate in the regular assessment; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subitem>
<ns0:subitem style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c09-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb/BB"><ns0:num value="BB">(BB)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subitem>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c0a-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VII"><ns0:num value="VII">(VII)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c0b-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII"><ns0:num value="VIII">(VIII)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0c-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based upon age appropriate transition assessments related to training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0d-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the transition services (including courses of study) needed to assist the child in reaching those goals; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0e-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> beginning not later than 1 year before the child reaches the age of majority under State law, a statement that the child has been informed of the child’s rights under this chapter, if any, that will transfer to the child on reaching the age of majority under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1415/m">section 1415(m) of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c0f-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Rule of construction</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c10-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c11-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the IEP Team to include information under 1 component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of such IEP.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c12-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Individualized education program team</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The term “individualized education program team” or “IEP Team” means a group of individuals composed of—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c13-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the parents of a child with a disability;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c14-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> not less than 1 regular education teacher of such child (if the child is, or may be, participating in the regular education environment);</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c15-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iii"><ns0:num value="iii">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> not less than 1 special education teacher, or where appropriate, not less than 1 special education provider of such child;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c16-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv"><ns0:num value="iv">(iv)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a representative of the local educational agency who—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c17-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is qualified to provide, or supervise the provision of, specially designed instruction to meet the unique needs of children with disabilities;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c18-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c19-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the local educational agency;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1a-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/v"><ns0:num value="v">(v)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results, who may be a member of the team described in clauses (ii) through (vi);</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1b-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/vi"><ns0:num value="vi">(vi)</ns0:num><ns0:content> at the discretion of the parent or the agency, other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the child, including related services personnel as appropriate; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1c-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/vii"><ns0:num value="vii">(vii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> whenever appropriate, the child with a disability.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1d-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C"><ns0:num value="C" class="bold">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> IEP Team attendance</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1e-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Attendance not necessary</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A member of the IEP Team shall not be required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1f-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Excusal</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c20-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c21-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c22-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/iii"><ns0:num value="iii" class="bold">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Written agreement and consent required</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c23-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/D"><ns0:num value="D" class="bold">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> IEP Team transition</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:uscDoc>

accepted.summary: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children (as appropriate) how it affects participation in appropriate activities, and for children with disabilities taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, benchmarks or short-term objectives; (II) measurable annual goals (including academic and functional goals) designed to meet needs resulting from the disability to enable involvement and progress in the general education curriculum and meet each other educational need resulting from the disability; (III) a description of how progress toward meeting annual goals will be measured and when periodic progress reports (such as quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with report cards) will be provided; (IV) a statement of special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services (based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable), and program modifications or supports for school personnel, to advance appropriately toward annual goals, be involved and make progress in the general education curriculum, participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in regular class and such activities; (VI) a statement of individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and if the IEP Team determines the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the alternate assessment selected is appropriate; (VII) the projected start date for services and modifications, and their anticipated frequency, location, and duration; and (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16 (updated annually), appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based on age-appropriate transition assessments and transition services needed to assist in reaching them, plus (beginning not later than 1 year before reaching the age of majority under State law) a statement that the child has been informed of rights under this chapter, if any, transferring on reaching majority under section 1415(m).

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including how the disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children (as appropriate) how it affects participation in appropriate activities, and for children with disabilities taking alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, benchmarks or short-term objectives; (II) measurable annual goals (including academic and functional goals) designed to meet needs resulting from the disability to enable involvement and progress in the general education curriculum and meet each other educational need resulting from the disability; (III) a description of how progress toward meeting annual goals will be measured and when periodic progress reports (such as quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with report cards) will be provided; (IV) a statement of special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services (based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable), and program modifications or supports for school personnel, to advance appropriately toward annual goals, be involved and make progress in the general education curriculum, participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in regular class and such activities; (VI) a statement of individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and if the IEP Team determines the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the alternate assessment selected is appropriate; (VII) the projected start date for services and modifications, and their anticipated frequency, location, and duration; and (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP in effect when the child is 16 (updated annually), appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based on age-appropriate transition assessments and transition services needed to assist in reaching them, plus (beginning not later than 1 year before reaching the age of majority under State law) a statement that the child has been informed of rights under this chapter, if any, transferring on reaching majority under section 1415(m).

oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (ii) Excusal

A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—

(I) the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and

(II) the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.
